ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD must screen all shareholders, directors and UBOs against (i) the Financial Intelligence Centre's Targeted Financial Sanctions list under s26A of the FIC Act; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated lists (Resolutions 1267/1988/1373, as implemented in South African law); (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list where EUR or USD correspondent clearing is used; (iv) the OFAC SDN list contractually, because SWIFT USD clearings and Alibaba Pay USD/EUR rails involve US and EU correspondent banks; and (v) the SARS tax-risk and anti-avoidance indicators. PEP determination follows the FIC Act definition of 'prominent influential person': current/former heads of state or government, senior ministers, judges, senior public officials, senior executives of state-owned entities, political party leaders, senior military officers and their family members and close associates. Screening must occur at onboarding, on any change of UBO or director, and on a six-monthly refresh cycle. Any 'prohibited/targeted' hit requires suspension of the transaction or business relationship, a report to the Financial Intelligence Centre, and internal escalation documented for FIC supervisory inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, www.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be rendered in Latin script. Names may be in any of the eleven official South African languages, but any non-Latin-script trading name must be transliterated into Latin letters for registration. The statutory suffix '(Pty) Ltd' or 'Proprietary Limited' is mandatory for a private company. The name must not be offensive, misleading, imply governmental or statutory sponsorship, or create confusing similarity with an existing registered name or trademark protected in South Africa.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall: (1) within 10 business days of the CIPC rejection notice, submit a formal written reconsideration request via the CIPC e-Services portal, addressing the specific statutory objection raised under s11 of the Companies Act; (2) if reconsideration fails, file a request for administrative review before the Companies Tribunal under s174 of the Companies Act within 60 days of the rejection notice, accompanied by the CIPC rejection letter, the proposed name, and supporting legal argument; (3) simultaneously prepare and, where commercially feasible, submit a new alternative name reservation application (CoR 9.2) to preserve registration momentum; and (4) if the name contains a prohibited or sensitive token, obtain prior written ministerial or sectoral regulatory consent (for example, the Prudential Authority with respect to bank/insurance words) and attach such consent to the re-application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. South African law requires a physical registered office address in the Republic where process may be served and company records are kept. A genuine virtual-office service providing a physical street address, mail handling, custody of statutory records and acceptance of process service may satisfy CIPC; however, a pure post-box or mail-forwarding arrangement will fail SARS, FIC and banking-sector substance expectations. For this ISIC 4791 B2B cross-border marketplace operating through Alibaba Pay and SWIFT rails, a hybrid arrangement is recommended: virtual registered office plus a compliance office address where UBO files, accounting records and sanctions-screening evidence are physically maintained and made available for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low in year one, estimated at approximately 10-15% annualized probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by CIPC, SARS or FIC, consistent with the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and the absence of a statutory license. The probability rises to 30-40% if CIPC beneficial-ownership filings are late, duplicate filings emerge, SWIFT wire typologies trigger FIC section 47H directives, or adverse media/PEP flags surface during correspondent-bank reviews.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for no par value and consideration is payable to the company's bank account at incorporation if capital is introduced.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscribers hereby adopt the Memorandum of Incorporation as filed with CIPC, and all shares issued are ratified and allotted to the initial subscribers as set out in the incorporation documents; (2) the registered office of the company shall be [physical address], South Africa, and a company secretary is appointed; (3) the following persons are appointed to the initial officer positions: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Compliance Officer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting; (4) the opening of a corporate bank account and the appointment of the first registered auditor, where required, are hereby approved. DATED this [day] day of [month] 20[year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for reservation of the proposed company name through CIPC online services, complete Form CoR 9.1, and pay the prescribed name reservation fee. Ensure the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing names and is not offensive or prohibited under the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Identity documents or passport copies of directors and incorporators
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a fresh name application with alternative names or submit an objection/appeal via CIPC form CoR 9.6 within the prescribed 30-day period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation and Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and legal counsel (attorney registered under Legal Practice Act 28 of 2014)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI setting out the rights, preferences and restrictions on shares, number and qualifications of directors, quorum and decision-making rules, and the audit and financial statements requirements. Ensure the MOI is consistent with the Companies Act and the company is a (Pty) Ltd with liability of shareholders limited.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC queries the MOI's compliance, revise the relevant clauses and resubmit the MOI with a compliance note; any inconsistency with the Act will be resolved in favour of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Notice of Incorporation to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CoR 14.1 together with the signed MOI and required declarations electronically through CIPC. Confirm the first directors' details, registered office and number of shares issued. Pay the official filing fee and the name reservation fee (if separate).
required_dossiers: CoR 15.1 Declaration of Solvency and Proportionality (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, undertake corrections to the scattered data, re-file the affected form within CIPC's e-services portal, and if necessary file an internal review request within the required time.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Register with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC and South African Revenue Service (SARS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from CIPC. Thereafter register the company for income tax, VAT (if turnover exceeds R1 million or voluntarily), Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF), and Skills Development Levy (SDL) through the SARS eFiling portal; obtain an Income Tax Reference Number and Tax Compliance Status PIN.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS flags the registration, correct the promoter details and resubmit the relevant registration forms; for CIPC certificate anomalies, lodge a rectification request with the CIPC customer contact centre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Directors and Officers, Open Bank Account and Adopt Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and the company's chosen commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, pass the first board resolution (as drafted above), allot shares, adopt bank mandates, appoint the chief executive, chief financial and compliance officers, open a corporate bank account in the company's name, and ensure minutes of the board meeting are signed and retained in the company minute book.
required_dossiers: Bank account application forms and FICA documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application, cure by providing a certified resolution of the directors, updated proof of residential address for directors, and taxpayer reference numbers; for governance defects, pass a corrective board resolution and restate the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Industrial and Environmental Licensing Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), and Local Municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the electronic B2B marketplace (ISIC 4791) does not require an industrial operating or manufacturing permit. Submit a compliance letter to the local municipality that the premises are used purely as offices or data operations; register and pay municipal rates and refuse/electrical charges; obtain environmental exemption confirmation under the EIA Regulations if no listed activity exists.
required_dossiers: Premises lease agreement or title deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality disputes the use, appeal with the zoning board; if DFFE requests an EIA, file a Part 2 environmental authorisation application or an exemption application under section 24G of NEMA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is applicable; an electronic B2B marketplace (ISIC 4791) is not classified as a licensed physical industry under South African law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA listed activity triggered for office/IT operations; if the premises host physical fulfilment warehousing, only waste management licensing under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office/data-centre wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge bylaws and the National Water Act, 1998; VOC emissions are not material, though any generator or cooling equipment must meet air emission standards under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 2004; waste handling must comply with WEEE regulations under the Waste Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the local fire authority (e.g., City of Cape Town Fire and Rescue or Johannesburg Emergency Management Services) for the registered office; electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC) issued by a registered electrician; structural load certificate if the building floor load exceeds residential limits; Occupational Health and Safety (OHS Act 85 of 1993) workplace clearance, including basic fire extinguishers, exit signage, and first-aid kits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd already incorporated under the Companies Act: (1) register for income tax with SARS via eFiling by submitting Form IT77 together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), CIPC registration certificate, directors' IDs and proof of physical address; SARS issues an income tax reference number (TIN). (2) Register for VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act using Form VAT101 if taxable supplies meet the compulsory threshold; a VAT101 number is allocated. (3) Obtain a customs code from SARS Customs if importing/exporting. For a non-resident foreign entity without a local presence but supplying electronic services to South African recipients, registration for VAT as a foreign vendor is compulsory once the annual threshold is exceeded; the same VAT101 eFiling channel is used without requiring CIPC registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box election; legal form determines classification. A (Pty) Ltd is automatically a resident company taxed at entity level. No hybrid mismatch elections are available; the anti-hybrid rules in the Income Tax Act apply coercively from 1 January 2021. Elective mechanisms relevant to indirect tax include the VAT grouping election under Section 47 of the VAT Act, which permits two or more corporate group members in South Africa to register as a single vendor.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period for compulsory local vendor registration; ZAR 50,000 for voluntary registration; non-resident suppliers of electronic services exceed ZAR 1,000,000 annual electronic services turnover to South African recipients
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time national fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping is currently in force. Electronic tax invoices are permitted if they meet the statutory particulars in Section 20 of the VAT Act. SARS is progressively implementing an e-invoicing framework and has the power to require prescribed data formats submitted through eFiling/API; exporters must retain all shipping and customs records for inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, goods supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated if they are exported from South Africa within 90 days of the date of supply, the exporter retains documentary proof of physical export, and the supply is made to the non-resident. Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under Section 11(2)(l) if the services are not supplied to a resident recipient and are physically rendered outside South Africa or not connected with South African property; a B2B cross-border platform service supplied to foreign business customers will generally qualify when the foreign customer is the sole recipient and the service is not consumed in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged with SARS Customs
Commercial invoice and tax invoice issued to the non-resident purchaser
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill showing physical removal from South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorised foreign-exchange dealer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow zero-rating and assess additional output VAT at 15% if the documentary proof is deficient. A 10% understatement penalty, 10% late-payment penalty and statutory interest apply under the Tax Administration Act; intentional evasion can trigger a penalty of up to 200% of the tax, retrospective clawback of refunds and input tax credits, and criminal prosecution for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) — Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting as the Exchange Control Authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a managed convertibility regime under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, administered by SARB FinSurv through authorised dealers. Current account transactions (trade in goods and services, interest, royalties, and dividends declared out of distributable reserves) are generally convertible against documentary proof without FinSurv pre-approval where within authorised dealer delegated limits. Capital account flows (inward foreign equity, inward/outward loans, direct investment) are permitted but strictly controlled: foreign equity capital requires registration on the company's non-resident share register and a capital import record with the authorised dealer; inward loans above the prevailing authorised dealer threshold (currently ZAR 50 million) require FinSurv approval. Profit remittance hurdles include: (i) dividend payments require audited or signed financial statements confirming distributable reserves, a SARS corporate income tax clearance, and a dividend tax withholding directive (20% statutory rate, treaty relief available on application to SARS); (ii) all outward remittances require correct BOP purpose codes and supporting commercial documentation; (iii) funds may not be remitted where the exporter has failed to repatriate export proceeds; (iv) remittances of royalties and service fees require a SARS tax directive covering the 15% royalty/interest withholding tax. Overall, the rand is convertible on current account with declared purpose, but capital account mobility is constrained by reporting, authorisation thresholds, and tax clearance gatekeeping.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 6(1), all proceeds from the export of goods and services must be paid into a South African authorised dealer account within 180 days from date of shipment (goods) or date of performance (services). The obligation is full repatriation: 100% of export proceeds must be surrendered to an authorised dealer, meaning they must be credited to the exporter's South African banking account; the proceeds are automatically converted to ZAR unless the exporter maintains an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with the authorised dealer, in which case the foreign currency may be retained for bona fide trade purposes. There is no statutory ratio mandating conversion of a percentage of proceeds into ZAR; the mandatory component is the complete inward repatriation into the South African banking system and the associated exchange control declaration and reporting by the authorised dealer to SARB FinSurv. For longer credit terms on capital goods, exporters may apply for extension or pre-approval; any unauthorised retention offshore or payment to an offshore non-authorised dealer account constitutes a contravention of the regulations and will trigger AML/exchange control penalties and loss of banking facilities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW. Legal constraints: an offshore electronic money institution (EMI) such as Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, or Airwallex is not an authorised dealer in foreign exchange under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933. A South African resident company may not lawfully collect or hold export proceeds through an offshore EMI because all export proceeds must be repatriated to a South African authorised dealer within 180 days. Retaining funds offshore in an EMI would constitute an unauthorised foreign currency account and violate Exchange Control Regulation 6(1)(a), exposing the entity to penalties, forced surrender, and criminal liability. Offshore EMI accounts are available only with explicit FinSurv dispensation for defined operational needs. Consequently, the B2B marketplace target rails (Alibaba_Pay and similar PSPs) must be structured as pass-through collection mechanisms into the South African authorised dealer account, or replaced by SWIFT wire collection directly into the SA bank account; any PSP aggregation model must be disclosed to the bank and approved as compliant under FICA and exchange control rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a South African incorporated (Pty) Ltd with in-country directors holding valid South African identification, remote digital onboarding is generally feasible using FICA-compliant biometric verification, electronic ID verification, and secure video interviews; physical attendance at a branch is normally not mandated. For structures with non-resident directors, 100% foreign ownership, or complex offshore beneficial ownership, Tier-1 South African banks typically require enhanced due diligence: physical or notarial identity verification of directors and UBOs, apostilled and legalised corporate documents, board resolutions, FATCA/CRS self-certifications, source-of-wealth evidence, and a recorded interview (in person or via secure video conference) with the relationship manager. Remote opening is therefore conditional on the ability to verify all directors and UBOs digitally; non-resident directors without a South African physical presence will almost always trigger a physical or notarised KYC mandate and may require the opening of the account through the bank's international desk or a foreign correspondent referral.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — foreign corporate shareholder(s) owning more than 25%, layered offshore ownership, or unresolved beneficial ownership register
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart; Certified Beneficial Ownership Register filed in terms of the Companies Act; certified passports/IDs of all natural UBOs and directors; notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation and memorandum of incorporation; board resolution appointing authorised signatories; source-of-funds evidence for initial capital (SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit slips, foreign bank statements, audited financial statements of the corporate shareholder); independent bank reference from a reputable foreign bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B marketplace payment flows — high transaction velocity, third-party settlement, e-wallet aggregation (Alibaba_Pay), or payments routed through non-bank PSPs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FICA-compliant merchant and buyer KYC files with risk-tiering; transaction monitoring and sanctions screening programme; underlying commercial contracts, platform order logs, commercial invoices, and settlement reconciliation reports; clear description of payment flow architecture and segregation of client funds; appointment of an FATCA/CRS and AML compliance officer of the company; quarterly suspicious transaction reporting framework; exchange control approval or authorised dealer acknowledgement of the PSP aggregation model; representation that all export proceeds are repatriated to the authorised dealer account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between invoicing party, beneficiary, and platform counterparty, or payments routed through affiliate entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated supplier and buyer contracts; board-approved treasury mandate and payment authority matrix; group transfer-pricing documentation (OECD-aligned, with SARS-relevant functional and risk analysis); detailed audit trail showing the commercial substance of each cross-border payment; evidence that the PSP arrangement is a pure pass-through with full reconciliation capability; customs import/export permits and bills of entry where physical goods are traded; SARS tax clearance certificate and VAT registration status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, adverse media, sanctions exposure, or counterparties resident in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and sanctions screening results (LSEG/World-Check or equivalent); adverse media due diligence report with outcome assessment; SARS tax clearance/PIN status; beneficial ownership declaration; enhanced monitoring plan covering periodic review; independent legal opinion or corporate due diligence report on each material counterparty; sworn affidavit as to the absence of prohibited conduct; commitment letter to maintain full transaction visibility to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign equity capital must be remitted by the non-resident shareholder via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for large value) to the entity's account at a South African authorised dealer, using the approved BOP purpose code for direct investment equity capital (SA BOP code 100 — direct investment into the reporting economy). The authorised dealer must receive a Compliance File containing the Share Subscription Agreement, board resolution approving the allotment, updated register of members reflecting the non-resident shareholding, FAIS/AML declarations, and the completed Inward Foreign Investment questionnaire; funds are credited to the Capital Escrow Account and thereafter transferred to the operating account once the bank confirms the non-resident status on the Capital Register. For inward loans from non-resident shareholders or third-party lenders, the loan must be documented and reported; authorised dealers may approve inward loans up to the prevailing monetary limit (currently ZAR 50 million) without FinSurv approval, with amounts above that threshold requiring a formal FinSurv application via the authorised dealer. The bank will record the proceeds in the Borrower's EMV / Loan Register; repayment of principal and interest is remittable subject to a SARS tax clearance via Form A and proof of the original inflow. Verification steps: (i) bank confirms the remitter is the same party as the shareholder/lender; (ii) BOP and EMV coding applied; (iii) exchange control forms completed; (iv) funds released to operations only after full KYC/AML clearance; (v) annual Financial Reporting Forms (Form C) submitted through the authorised dealer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The B2B platform will disburse cross-border trade payments through the following cleared rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier/vendor payments, supported by commercial invoices, contracts, and SARS tax clearance; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections issued/negotiated by the authorised dealer for goods imports, requiring the pro-forma invoice, insurance/cargo documents, and customs Bill of Entry; (iii) high-volume seller payouts via MT101/ISO 20022 batch files for SME merchants, with each payment subject to sanctions screening and FICA verification of the beneficiary; and (iv) local ZAR clearing via the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS)/Real-Time Clearing infrastructure for domestic disbursements. For service fees, royalties, and payments to foreign contractors, the remitter must present a SARS directive confirming the correct withholding tax treatment (royalty/interest at 15% or applicable treaty rate) and an approved BOP purpose code; no outward payment may be made for purely speculative or capital preservation purposes. The authorised dealer will also require written confirmation that export proceeds have been repatriated in compliance with Regulation 6(1) before permitting outsized or high-frequency trade disbursements. Payments must be made directly to the true commercial beneficiary; third-party settlement arrangements must be pre-approved and fully documented to avoid classification as an unauthorised outward transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (DFCs) with an authorised dealer, covering confirmed underlying commercial exposure in goods or services, with tenor matched to the underlying transaction and allowable tolerance for invoice variability

Cross-currency swaps with an authorised dealer or qualifying counterparty, permitted for hedging long-term foreign-currency liabilities or receivables evidenced by commercial contracts, subject to FinSurv reporting and documentation of the underlying exposure

FX options (premium-paid, non-speculative strategies) with an authorised dealer to hedge import or export invoice exposure, covered by documented commercial transactions and subject to bank exposure limits
JSE-listed USD/ZAR currency futures for short-term, non-speculative hedging of committed trade flows, with regulated margining and no deliverable settlement risk

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not available to South African residents onshore for hedging ZAR exposure without specific SARB FinSurv dispensation; non-resident counterparties may square offshore NDF markets only, while the ZA entity must use onshore deliverable instruments through authorised dealers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 2008, Section 33; Companies Regulation 34)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Republic of South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of ZAR 500 (approx. USD 27) per month or part of a month; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers CIPC deregistration (strike-off) proceedings under Section 82; a deregistered company ceases to exist and directors may incur personal liability for debts incurred while trading non-compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (BO) Register annual declaration and change notification (Companies Act 2008, Section 56; Companies Amendment Regulations 2022/2023)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) online Beneficial Ownership module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, together with the annual return; any change in beneficial ownership, including a shareholding transfer, must be filed within 30 days of the transaction or event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC may issue a compliance notice and levy administrative fines; failure to file or knowingly filing false beneficial ownership data is an offence under the Companies Act carrying a fine of up to ZAR 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months, with continuing non-compliance capable of grounding strike-off review and director personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) with independent audit or review (Companies Act 2008, Sections 29-31; Regulation 28)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and shareholders; AFS retained at the registered office and provided to SARS within the corporate income tax process (private companies are not required to file AFS with CIPC unless the MOI or a public interest score so triggers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the company's financial year-end; audit or independent review report must accompany AFS where prescribed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare and approve AFS within 6 months commit an offence under Sections 30 and 216 (fine up to ZAR 10,000 and/or 12 months' imprisonment); CIPC may issue compliance notices; shareholders may apply to a court for an order compelling preparation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) or unanimous written consent in lieu (Companies Act 2008, Section 61)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; minutes filed in the company's minute book and maintained for inspection at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation, thereafter not more than 15 months after the previous AGM; a private company may dispense with the AGM where the MOI permits and all shareholders consent in writing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty for a private company, but shareholder complaint to CIPC is available for irregular governance; failure to observe AGM or MOI requirements may support director removal proceedings and shareholder relief.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where the company's Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more for the financial year; PIS between 100 and 349 requires an independent review unless the MOI mandates an audit; PIS below 100 requires neither audit nor review absent a MOI or regulatory requirement. PIS is calculated from number of employees, third-party liabilities, turnover, and members entitled to voting rights.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for entities with public accountability or mandatory audit; IFRS for SMEs for eligible small and medium entities; South African Statements of GAAP are discontinued and do not constitute a statutory framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each (Pty) Ltd must file a Beneficial Ownership Declaration with CIPC at each annual return anniversary and must notify CIPC of any change in beneficial ownership, including shareholding transfers, within 30 days of the change; the Beneficial Ownership Register must remain synchronised with the securities register and be physically available on-site for CIPC inspection; a person who acquires or disposes of a beneficial interest in securities must notify the company within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150-600 per annum (CIPC-registered office / company secretarial retainer, Johannesburg or Cape Town market)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000-8,000 per annum for a certified independent audit of a small-to-mid B2B platform entity; independent review (PIS 100-349) generally USD 800-2,500 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket statutory tax holiday. Preferential effective tax rates arise from Special Economic Zone (SEZ) rules (15% corporate rate for qualifying SEZ companies), the s11D research & development deduction (up to 150%), accelerated capital allowances for manufacturing plant and machinery under s12B/s12C, and s12H learnership deductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Corporate Income Tax Return; submitted electronically via the South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal, either by the entity or an authorised tax practitioner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual return due no later than 12 months after the fiscal year-end, subject to the filing date allocated by SARS in the annual filing-season notice; provisional tax returns are not a substitute for the ITR14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number, legal entity name, country of incorporation, tax reference number, and financial year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the South African (Pty) Ltd registration number; non-resident beneficial owners are separately identified through shareholder disclosure and the annual Beneficial Ownership registers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from B2B marketplace commissions, listing fees, transaction facilitation charges, and any ancillary trading receipts sourced in South Africa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All platform income attributable to a South African resident company or permanent establishment (PE) is fully taxable at 27%; no DTA relief is available on local trading profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income including certain foreign dividends, interest and capital protection arrangements recognised by statute.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividends and interest may be exempt or credited only if evidenced by non-resident tax residency certificates and the relevant SARS notification; otherwise taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operational expenditure, cost of sales, s11D R&D expenditure, s12C allowances, lease costs, employment costs, and arm's-length adjustments for connected-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only for expenses actually incurred in the production of income; payments to offshore connected persons require a transfer-pricing adjustment and supporting economic-substance documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed loss available for set-off under the loss-carryforward regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned company may use assessed losses only if the trade giving rise to the loss is carried on in South Africa; losses are subject to the five-year carryforward limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying available assessed losses and all statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate strictly in ZAR; foreign exchange differences arising from foreign-denominated revenue must be applied in accordance with s24I.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final headline corporate tax computed at 27% of taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no separate corporate-level filing obligation; the tax is assessed on the ZA-resident operating entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foreign Tax Credits and s6quat Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign taxes paid on foreign-sourced income included in the taxable income and permitted by the SARS foreign-tax-credit rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent company cannot claim the foreign tax credit individually; the credit belongs to the South African company that paid the foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all affected transactions with connected persons, transfer pricing method applied, and contemporaneous documents in your possession.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent/affiliate transactions must individually and in aggregate be disclosed; document the tested party, benchmarking, and economic substance basis for the arm's-length price.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act (TAA), escalating monthly based on taxable income. Interest is levied on unpaid tax at the SARS prescribed rate (currently around the prime overdraft rate plus 2%). An understatement penalty under section 222 ranges from 0% to 150% of the understated tax, depending on whether the conduct was a reasonable care, substantial understatement, gross negligence, or intentional tax evasion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 – Provisional Tax Return; submitted electronically via SARS eFiling.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual (each tax year has two mandatory provisional periods; a voluntary third top-up period is available after the first interim and before final assessment).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional payment due within 6 months of the start of the tax year; second provisional payment due on or before the last business day of the tax year; voluntary third top-up payment may be made within 7 months of the end of the tax year or within 6 months of final assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A – Estimated Current-Year Assessed Loss / Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimate of the current year's taxable income or assessed loss before offsetting available losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Estimate must include all South Africa-source revenue and be based on realistic, not artificially low, profit projections; avoid underestimation to prevent additional penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 27% on the estimated taxable income, reduced by any present-year payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent company guarantees, loans, or advances considered for interest withholding and TP purposes are incorporated in the provisional liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First and second provisional payments already made for the assessment year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not reduce the provisional liability except under a valid treaty or section 6quat foreign tax credit regime, supported by TRCs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount payable with the provisional return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The full amount must be paid in ZAR via electronic payment; SARS will charge interest and penalties on any shortfall.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under-estimation of taxable income triggers, in addition to interest, a penalty under the Fourth Schedule of the Income Tax Act if the estimate is not based on fair and reasonable assumptions. Failure to submit provisional returns is subject to monthly administrative non-compliance penalties and can lead to criminal prosecution for non-compliance under the TAA.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (final dividend withholding tax, payable by the South African company as withholding agent).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced or exempt DWT under a double taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must complete and submit to the paying entity (i) a valid Declaration for reduced dividend withholding tax (withholding agent's copy), (ii) an actual tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home-country revenue authority, and (iii) evidence of beneficial ownership. The documents must be lodged before the dividend is paid; otherwise the company is statutorily required to withhold at 20%. Where a DTA provides a lower rate, a refund may be claimed via SARS once the documentation is corrected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax rates for non-residents: 15% on royalties and 15% on interest; no deduction at source for SA-source service fees other than royalties and interest. Under applicable DTAs, interest rates may be reduced to 0%–10% depending on the payment (government/government-owned body or financial institution), and royalty rates are commonly reduced to 0%–12.5%. Treaty relief requires the same TRC and beneficial-ownership declarations, retained by the withholding agent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: SARS Interpretation Note 69 and the TAA require contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation where the aggregate cross-border connected-party transactions exceed ZAR 10 million per year; a Master File is expected for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue above ZAR 7 billion, and a Country-by-Country Report is required for groups with consolidated revenue above ZAR 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have a separate GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations code; the equivalent substance doctrine is applied through common-law substance-over-form, s31 (transfer pricing and permanent establishment protection), s6/ CFC rules, and the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under section 103 of the Income Tax Act. A non-resident-owned South African company must demonstrate actual office functions, employees, assets, and risk,s carried on in South Africa to sustain treaty benefits and transfer-pricing positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting B2B marketplace platform commission revenue, concealing bank accounts receiving Alibaba Pay or SWIFT wire transfers, issuing false invoices, or fabricating expenses to reduce taxable income in the ITR14.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 222 TAA understatement penalty of 150% of the understated tax for intentional tax evasion; 100% for gross negligence; compounded interest on the full past-due tax; criminal conviction may render the company liable to a higher fine and imprisonment of responsible persons. Additionally, SARS can void false tax returns and issue a statutory assessment on the best available information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers who knowingly participate in evasion are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties under TAA sections governing senior management liability; SARS may prohibit their departure from South Africa via exit-control procedures, seize personal assets, and institute criminal charges leading to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a lavishly structured company with no physical office, no employees, no activities other than receiving platform income, and using nominee directors solely to funnel B2B commissions to a foreign parent or to access a DTA rate without real economic presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will apply the GAAR under section 103 to disregard the artificial transaction, re-allocate the profits to the substantive person, and impose an understatement penalty of up to 150% of the additional assessment. If treaty relief is claimed on the basis of an artificial PE, SARS may deny the DTA benefit and impose interest as well as repayment of any refunded dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Companies Act imposes personal liability on directors who fail to prevent reckless trading or knowingly allow the company to operate as a vehicle for tax evasion; in tax enforcement, directors may be joined as co-defendants, placed under civil restraint, have travel rights revoked, and be disqualified from acting as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FICA Non-Compliance in Payment Processing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving B2B marketplace proceeds through electronic payment rails and distributing payouts without registering the company as an accountable institution with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC), without conducting customer due diligence, or without reporting cash transactions above ZAR 49 999 and suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, the FIC may impose administrative penalties: up to ZAR 10 million for each material non-compliance episode; criminal conviction may lead to a fine up to ZAR 50 million and/or imprisonment up to 10 years for continuous and intentional breach, including aiding money laundering through platform gateways.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, especially the appointed compliance officer, bear personal criminal liability if the institution cannot prove the adoption of a compliant anti-money-laundering framework; directors may additionally be disqualified from holding office and be subject to a SARS/FIC joint enforcement action, with assets frozen pending proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive Transfer Pricing and Missing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging an artificially low arm's-length commission to an offshore affiliate, entering into circular financing arrangements, paying excessive management fees to a foreign parent, or failing to produce Local File / Master File documentation when the annual connected-party transaction value surpasses the SARS threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will adjust taxable income to an arm's-length result under section 31 and assess additional tax, interest, and a 100% understatement penalty for gross negligence; if the lack of documentation is intentional, the penalty may be 150%. SARS may also impose a separate TAA non-compliance penalty for failure to retain or produce required records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the ITR14 without verifying transfer-pricing records are personally exposed to civil liability for causing losses to the fiscus; in egregious cases a court can pierce the corporate veil, making directors liable for the adjusted tax liability and precluding them from leaving South Africa until the debt is settled.
